interest: Shows 1931 Japanese zaibatsu negotiating directly for Persian opium, tracked closely by State and the new Bureau of Narcotics.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.503191, spanning April to July 1931) documents the United States diplomatic corps' investigation into emerging Japanese commercial, industrial, and financial interests in Persia (Iran), with a sharp focus on the international opium trade. The correspondence begins when Charles C. Hart, the American Minister at Teheran, transmits local Persian press accounts detailing the formation of the 'San-Kio Syndicate'—comprising Japanese firms Sankyo, Okura, and Mitsubishi—which sought to purchase Persian raw opium from the state monopoly holder and foster wider bilateral trade, alongside reports of an ambitious Perso-Balkan cultural and commercial exhibition in Osaka. Recognizing the sensitive implications for international drug control, the Department of State coordinated intelligence between the American Legation in Teheran, the American Embassy in Tokyo (where Counselor Edwin L. Neville detailed Japan's colonial opium monopolies in Formosa and Dairen and domestic morphine production), and the U.S. Treasury Department's Bureau of Narcotics, establishing a continuous exchange of reporting between Washington, Tokyo, and Teheran.

subfiles.about: Reports on Teheran press accounts regarding Japanese capital turning toward Persia for investment and commercial promotion.
subfiles.summary: Minister Hart reports Japanese financiers investing in Persia, enclosing press articles on a planned Perso-Balkan exhibition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 529 from Charles C. Hart on Japanese Economic Interest in Persia

subfiles.about: Details the formation of a commercial syndicate by Japanese firms San-Kio, Okura, and Mitsubishi to negotiate an opium deal with Persia's monopoly holder and expand trade.
subfiles.from: Setareh'ye Djhane and Ettela'at (translated by U.S. Legation, Teheran)
subfiles.summary: Press translations: Japan's San-Kio, Okura, and Mitsubishi formed a syndicate to buy Persian opium and expand bilateral trade.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 529: Press Translations on the 'San-Kio Syndicate' and Opium Trade
subfiles.to: Department of State (enclosed with Despatch No. 529)

subfiles.about: Describes plans by the Foreign Trade Museum in Osaka to host a Perso-Balkan cultural and trade exhibition in October 1931.
subfiles.summary: Translation: Osaka's Foreign Trade Museum planned an October 1931 Perso-Balkan exhibition with regional governments and school art exchanges.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2 to Despatch No. 529: Translation of Article from Iran on the Perso-Balkan Exhibition in Osaka
subfiles.to: Department of State (enclosed with Despatch No. 529)

subfiles.about: Instructs the Legation at Teheran to monitor and submit additional reports on Japanese commercial activities in Persia, particularly regarding opium transactions.
subfiles.summary: State tells Teheran to keep reporting on Japanese business in Persia, especially opium transactions.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 85 from Department of State to American Minister at Teheran

subfiles.about: Transmits a confidential copy of Teheran Despatch No. 529 and its enclosures regarding Japanese interest in Persian opium to the Commissioner of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: State alerts Treasury's Narcotics Bureau to press reports of a Japanese syndicate's Persian opium purchase.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to Treasury Department Regarding Persian Opium Trade
subfiles.to: The Secretary of the Treasury (Attention: Bureau of Narcotics)

subfiles.about: Directs the Tokyo Embassy to report on Japanese economic enterprises in Persia and assess the likelihood of direct trade and opium purchases.
subfiles.summary: State asks Tokyo to investigate Japanese business ventures and opium purchases in Persia.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 109 from Department of State to American Ambassador at Tokyo

subfiles.about: Analyzes Japanese government opium purchases in Formosa and Dairen, domestic morphine manufacturing, and the business profiles of Sankyo, Mitsubishi, and Okura.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville (Counselor of Embassy, Tokyo, for the Ambassador)
subfiles.summary: Neville reports Japan's Formosa and Dairen opium monopolies and morphine makers have long bought Persian opium, naming Sankyo, Mitsubishi, and Okura as key firms now considering direct trade.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 268 from Edwin L. Neville on Japanese Trade with Persia and Opium Purchases

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 268 regarding Japanese opium monopolies and Persian trade to the Bureau of Narcotics.
subfiles.summary: State forwards Treasury's Narcotics chief Tokyo's report on Japanese pharmaceutical firms' Persian opium procurement.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Acting Secretary of the Treasury Transmitting Tokyo Report
subfiles.to: The Acting Secretary of the Treasury (Attention: Bureau of Narcotics)

subfiles.about: Transmits Tokyo Despatch No. 268 to the Teheran Legation and requests direct cross-reporting between the diplomatic posts.
subfiles.summary: State shares Tokyo's findings on Japanese opium procurement with Teheran, asking future reports go directly to Tokyo too.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 96 from Department of State to American Minister at Teheran
